To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chromogranin-A (CgA)-containing granules in constitutively secretory COS-7 cells exhibit a calcium-dependent trafficking and exocytosed in response to calcium.
CgA induces a granule biogenesis that is characterized by Ca(2+)(2+)-dependent vesicle trafficking and Ca(2+) and actin-dependent exocytosis.
chromogranin-A induces the biogenesis and Ca(2+) and actin-dependent trafficking of granules with regulated exocytosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of the biogenesis, transport and release of neuroendocrine vesicles in constitutively secretory COS-7 cells.
the molecular mechanism of neuroendocrine secretion and its dysregulation in neurodegenerative disorders.
the mechanisms underlying the biogenesis of neuroendocrine granules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

CgA induces a reorganization of the cytoskeleton and its association with the membrane, and that this reorganization is essential to the generation of a granule that is endowed with a typical granule morphology and a regulated exocytosis.
CgA induces a reorganization of the constitutive vesicles to form secretory granules endowed with typical dynamics.
CgA is not only a major component of the granule core, but also plays a crucial role in the biogenesis, the transport, and the Ca(2+) evoked exocytotic release of secretory granule.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neuroendocrin factor CgA can recruit cytoskeleton-, Ca2+-, and GTP-binding proteins in constitutvely secreting COS-1 cells to generate granules endowed with typical dynamics of secretory granule.
CgA induces granulogenesis in constitutively-secretory cells by recruiting cytoskeleton-, actin-, and GTP-binding proteins.

the neuroendocrinological factor CgA, by interacting with the cytoskeleton and the actin-based molecular motors, induces the biogenesis and the trafficking of granules endowed with typical dynamics, exocytotic and Ca(2+) sensitivity properties of neuroendocrinological cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CgA is able to induce granule biogenesis and trafficking in constitutively secretory cells.
